label: 3v
quote: Nimm das Axiom: Absolut richtige Prophezeiungen sind unmög- lich (auch für den Laplaceschen Weltgeist?)
english: Take the axiom: absolutely correct prophecies are impossible (even for Laplace's world-spirit?)
topic: Philosophical notes on the foundations of mathematics: Kant's question, contradictions, Lindelöf's rejection of aleph_1, mathematics and philosophy, the 'ignorabimus', who understood Helmholtz and Einstein, prophecy, and why simple special problems such as the four-colour problem are hard.

triage.modern_statement: This is not a well-posed mathematical problem. It is a philosophical proposal to treat 'absolutely correct prophecies are impossible' as an axiom, and to ask whether the axiom would hold even for Laplace's demon, an intellect that knows the full state of the universe and all its laws. The closest modern version asks whether a deterministic universe can contain a physical device, or a predictor that is part of that universe, able to correctly predict every future fact about it, including facts about itself.
triage.answered_by: Hilbert never turned this into a formal problem, and it is not among his 23 problems or the 24th problem. Later work does address the formal version, though no source links that work to this note. Karl Popper's 'Indeterminism in Quantum Physics and in Classical Physics' (1950) argued that even classical physics does not let a predictor make complete predictions that include itself. David Wolpert's 'Physical limits of inference' (Physica D 237, 2008, pp. 1257–1281; arXiv:0708.1362) proved impossibility theorems for 'inference devices' that sit inside the universe they predict.

evidence.claim: Wolpert (Physica D, 2008) presents existence and impossibility results for physical devices that observe, predict or recall ('inference devices'). In a limited sense, these results show Laplace was wrong to claim that even a classical, non-chaotic universe's future can be predicted without error.
Wolpert, 'Physical limits of inference', Physica D 237 (2008) 1257–1281, doi 10.1016/j.physd.2008.03.040. One result is that no universe can contain more than one 'strong inference device'.
Wolpert and coauthors later formalized two 'Laplace's Demon theorems'. In these, a negation probe shows that certain kinds of complete inference are impossible.
In 'Indeterminism in Quantum Physics and in Classical Physics', Karl Popper used Laplace's demon to argue against 'scientific' determinism, even within classical physics.

triage.why: The entry is a philosophical aside on a page of philosophical notes. It proposes an 'axiom' about prophecy and asks whether it would bind Laplace's demon, but it does not state a mathematical problem. It is not one of Hilbert's published problems. The idea was later formalized and partly answered: Popper (1950) argued that self-prediction is impossible even in classical physics, and Wolpert (2008) proved diagonal-style impossibility theorems for predictors embedded in their own universe. None of the sources I found link that work to Hilbert's note. Work on limits of inference continues in a small niche, but I can't tell from these sources whether it counts as an active research area. Confidence is medium because the note is vague.
